item.title: Man continuing to be questioned in relation to Michael Gaine murder investigation
item.description: A man remains in garda custody this lunchtime, in relation to the investigation into the murder of Michael Gaine. The man, who is aged in his 50s, was arrested in Tralee at around 7.30 this morning, and continues to be questioned. Gardaí have not named the man but Radio Kerry has learned that he is US citizen Michael Kelley. item.title: Over €12.2 million allocated to healthcare capital projects in Kerry
item.description: Over 12.2 million euro (€12,248,520) has been allocated to healthcare infrastructure projects in Kerry under the proposed 2026 HSE capital plan. University Hospital Kerry (UHK) will get the lion’s share of the funding while, €392,980 has been allocated towards the design feasibility stage of a new ambulance station at Caherciveen Community Hospital. item.title: Kenmare councillor urges people not to speculate online and be considerate of Michael Gaine’s family
item.description: A Kenmare councillor has appealed for sensitivity for the family of Michael Gaine. It comes as a man in his 50s has been arrested for questioning in relation to Mr Gaine’s murder. The 56-year-old farmer was reported missing from his home outside Kenmare last March; the case was upgraded to a homicide investigation in late April. item.title: SNA protest in Killarney will still go ahead as campaigners say clarity is needed
item.description: Clarity is still needed on the situation for SNAs going forward. That’s according to Jackie Coffey, special needs assistant in Fossa National School. Fossa NS was one of a number of Kerry schools which had been due to lose SNAs for the next school year, before the government’s announcement that no SNA cuts would be taking place this year. item.title: Kerry county councillor slams level of mobile blackspots across the county
item.description: A Kerry county councillor has said the level of mobile blackspots across the county is unacceptable. Fianna Fáil Cllr Norma Moriarty said the issue is particularly bad in the Coars-Kilognaveen-Filmore area. She requested that Kerry County Council write to Vodafone and Com Reg seeking a detailed report on what is required to improve mobile phone coverage. item.title: Kerry venue has been named as one of Ireland’s best at the 2026 SaveMyDay Irish Wedding Venue Awards
item.description: A Kerry venue has been named as one of Ireland’s best at the 2026 SaveMyDay Irish Wedding Venue Awards Cromane’s Jacks’ Coastguard Restaurant has been named as Best Restaurant Wedding Venue at the awards. The annual awards, hosted by popular wedding venue platform SaveMyDay, honour the most‑loved wedding venues across the country, with winners chosen entirely by the public for the first time. item.title: HSE boss says it'll take time to restore public confidence in CAHMS in Kerry
item.description: The CEO of the Health Service Executive admits it will take quite a time to restore public confidence in CAHMS in Kerry. It's in the wake of the publication of damning reviews into services in both the north and south of the county. item.title: Minister Warns Against Fulfilling Ireland v Israel Fixture
item.description: Minister for Sport, Patrick O'Donovan has warned that Ireland would be the "big loser" if the upcoming Nations League games against Israel weren't fulfilled. The Republic of Ireland have been drawn to face Israel in the men's Nations League, with games scheduled for September and October. Shamrock Rovers manager Stephen Bradley and Shelbourne boss Joey O'Brien are among those calling for a boycott of the fixtures. item.title: Tralee-Native Leonard Set For Ireland EuroBasket Debut
item.description: Tralee-native Ryan Leonard has been included in the final 12-man Irish squad and could make his FIBA EuroBasket debut during next weekend's 2029 Pre-Qualifiers against Azerbaijan and Luxembourg. The Limerick Sport Eagles player will be joined by Jordan Blount of Flexachem KCYMS and another former Tralee Warriors player, Rap Buivydas who now plays with Belfast Star.
